svg.aria-label: Two columns: tools priced per seat, where self-hosting pays back almost at once, and tools priced per usage or paid in on-call time, where it usually does not

g.text: PRICED PER SEAT
Pays back almost at once
The bill grows with headcount. One server does not.
Git, issues and CI
Airtable-style databases
Docs, wiki and notes
Automation and agents
Status pages and uptime checks
Forgejo — one binary, idles near 100 MB
NocoDB — over a Postgres you already run
Outline, Docmost
n8n — the workflows we publish run on this
Uptime Kuma
Cost moves from per-person to one line on a hosting bill.
PRICED PER USAGE, PAID IN ON-CALL
Usually does not
The licence is free. The engineer running it is not.
Metrics, logs and traces
The production database
Object storage with a CDN
Anything that pages someone at 03:00
Kubernetes, before you need two nodes
below roughly 50 hosts, hosted wins on published models
managed Postgres is the thing worth paying for
an S3 clone is easy; being its SLA is not
if nobody is on call, do not own it
one node and Compose carries further than people expect
Savings here arrive around 200 hosts, not before.
The line between the two columns moves with your headcount and your volume.
list prices checked September 2026
